copyright: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Highlands, Scotland (© Scotland: The Big Picture/Minden Pictures)
description: As Britain's only native squirrel species, red squirrels thrive in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park. An important refuge, the park offers ancient Caledonian pine forests and newer conifer woodlands, with plentiful habitat and food for squirrels foraging for Scots pine seeds, nuts, and other tasty morsels year-round. In today's image, a red squirrel is perched amid warm orange and yellow leaves, looking right at home as it ponders its next move in the Scottish Highlands.

Today's image shows the gradual coiling of a young fiddlehead's tip, echoing the geometric patterns seen throughout nature. In math, the Fibonacci sequence follows a similar progression, each number formed by adding the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, and so on. Today is Fibonacci Day, chosen for the numbers of the date (11/23) to honor the sequence. Eventually the young fern frond shown here will unfurl as it grows, but elsewhere in the plant world, the sequence will continue to appear in the spiraling arrangements of sunflower heads, pinecones, succulents, and pineapples.

copyright: The chapel and hermitage of Santa Justa in Cantabria, Spain (© Tramont_ana/Getty Images)
description: Tucked into the cliffs of northern Spain's rugged coastline, the 16th-century Hermitage of Santa Justa seen in today's image overlooks the crashing waves of the Cantabrian Sea. Built partly into the rock and associated with relics of Saints Justa and Rufina, the small chapel eventually became a pilgrimage site, its sheltered stone walls creating a remarkable contrast with the powerful waves and rocky cliffs surrounding it.

copyright: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France (© Siripong Kaewla-iad/Getty Images)
description: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches, and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by ancient Greeks and long connected to the Italian royal House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, that layered past remains visible throughout the coastal city in the south of France, where old-world architecture meets the blue Mediterranean waters and sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.

copyright: Diving humpback whale, Kvaloya, Troms, Northern Norway (© Espen Bergersen/Minden Pictures)
description: Off the coast of Kvaløya in Troms, Northern Norway, humpback whales move through the cold Arctic waters in search of a proper feast. They visit this region during the winter months, following migrating herring into the fjords. Humpbacks are famous for bubble-net feeding, a remarkable hunting technique in which whales blow rings of bubbles to corral fish before lunging upward, open-mouthed, to catch their prey. In today's image, a humpback slips beneath the icy waves under a glowing pastel sky, capturing a moment of tranquility in Norway's wild north.

copyright: The "Body of Knowledge" sculpture by Jaume Plensa at Goethe University in Frankfurt, Germany (© Todamo/Shutterstock)
description: It's World Philosophy Day, when big thinkers gather to discuss life's eternal mysteries. To celebrate, today's image features the "Body of Knowledge" sculpture at Goethe University in Frankfurt, Germany, which molds steel letters from eight different alphabets into a human form. Spanish artist Jaume Plensa explains: "Our body is the home of the spirit. The place in which ideas live." On World Philosophy Day, we're all encouraged to look beyond easy answers and explore the questions that shape us, and the world around us.

copyright: Pair of barn owls (© Zahoor Salmi/Getty Images)
description: These barn owls, bathed in evening light, are waiting for the hunt to begin. As night falls, these birds of prey swoop into action, listening for tiny movements in grass or leaves made by mice and voles. Their heart-shaped faces help funnel sound into some of the sharpest ears in the animal kingdom. This allows them to locate their prey with pinpoint precision in the dark before swooping silently, their soft feathers muffling their approach. In autumn, young barn owls strike out to find their own territories. As the nights grow longer, you might spot them earlier in the evening, gliding over fields in search of supper.
